title: Design and Operation of Shared Machine Learning Clusters on Campus
problem: Academic GPU clusters must be shared equitably among many users with diverse ML workloads, but existing cluster management solutions are designed for large industrial settings and do not address the operational challenges specific to campus environments: limited staffing, heterogeneous hardware, fair multi-user resource allocation, and incident management at small scale.
motivation: Universities are investing heavily in GPU clusters to support growing large ML model workloads, and ineffective sharing leads to poor utilization and inequitable access; there is no full-stack solution tailored to campus settings with constrained IT resources.
method: SING provides a four-layer extensible architecture for shared GPU cluster management: a hardware/infrastructure layer (automated configuration and monitoring), a resource scheduling layer (fair allocation policies across users and jobs), an interface layer (user-facing job submission and access controls), and an operations layer (incident detection, logging, and management). The system is designed to minimize maintenance costs with limited staffing by automating routine operations, and to optimize utilization through workload-aware scheduling policies.
key_novelty: A full-stack campus GPU cluster management system with four extensible architectural layers tailored to the operational realities of academic environments (limited staffing, diverse users, heterogeneous hardware).
contributions: SING: a four-layer full-stack solution for shared GPU cluster management on campus
Analysis of real-world usage patterns and incident management strategies from deployment experience
Resource allocation policies balancing utilization and fairness for diverse academic ML workloads
Open-source release of SING resources to support similar academic cluster deployments

metrics.other: improved utilization and reduced maintenance costs in real deployment (specific numbers not in abstract)

baselines: existing GPU cluster management solutions (not specified)
limitations: Performance improvements are measured in a specific campus deployment context and may not generalize to all academic settings; quantitative results not stated in abstract.
primary_theme: full-stack shared GPU cluster management for academic environments
